Guidance & outlook: Consequently, the Company reported a Profit Before Tax of INR 1,092.34 lakhs in FY 2025-26, as compared to INR 981.29 lakhs in FY 2024 -25.
The Earnings Per Share (EPS) stood at INR 8.93 in FY 2025-26, as compared to INR 9.78 in FY 2024-25.

Growth & demand: During FY 2025-26, the Company reported Revenue from Operations of INR 4,936.53 Lakhs, registering a robust growth of approximately 88% over the previous year.

Profit Before Tax increased to INR 1,092.34 Lakhs, while Profit After Tax stood at INR 805.95 Lakhs, reflecting the Company's continued focus on sustainable and profitable growth through operational excellence and disciplined execution.
Remarks Revenue Growth 88.25% 10.56% 735.89% Yes Significant increase in business volumes following the strategic transition in the business model.
Margins & costs: EBITDA Margin contracted by approximately 19.86 per centage points (from 43.52% to 23.66%) and PAT Margin by approximately 11.65 percentage points (from 27.98% to 16.33%), while absolute EBITDA grew to INR 1,167.84 Lakhs and PAT to INR 805.95 Lakhs, demonstrating sustained operational strength and improved earnings despite the change in the revenue model.
EBITDA Margin 23.66% 43.52% -45.68% Yes Moderated due to the change in revenue composition under the Purchase & Sale business model.

Consequently, although both revenue and material costs increased significantly, the Company achieved higher absolute revenue, EBITDA and Profit After Tax, while EBITDA and Net Profit Margins moderated on a percentage basis due to the changed revenue composition.
Capex & expansion: Opportunities • Expansion of the Indian pharmaceutical industry. • Growing demand for solvent recycling and sustainable manufacturing. • Import substitution opportunities. • Capacity expansion supported by IPO proceeds.

Going forward, the Company intends to continue focusing on: • Expansion of business volumes. • New customer acquisition. • Product diversification. • Capacity enhancement. • Export opportunities. • Operational excellence. • Cost optimisation. • Sustainable manufacturing practices.

Cash generated during the year was primarily utilised for: • Working capital requirements. • Expansion of business operations. • Repayment of borrowings. • Capital expenditure. • Investment in manufacturing infrastructure.
Balance sheet & cash: Debt Service Coverage Ratio 3.23 1.26 156.35% Yes Continued to reflect strong debt repayment capability.

The Company derives a significant portion of its revenue from operations and trade receivables from related parties (approximately 52% of revenue and approximately 55% of trade receivables outstanding as at March 31, 2026, per Note 33 to the financial statements).

Key Audit Matters Auditor's Responses 1 Concentration of Revenue and Trade Receivables from Related Parties (Refer Note 41 to the financial statements) The Company derives approximately 52% of its revenue from operations and approximately 55% of its trade receivables outstanding as at 31st March, 2026 from related parties (group entities).
Risks & challenges: Threats • Volatility in crude oil and chemical prices. • Changes in environmental regulations. • Global economic uncertainties. • Supply chain disruptions. • Changes in government policies affecting the chemical industry.
Competition Risk The specialty chemicals industry is highly competitive, with competition from both organised and unorganised market participants.

The Company's risk management framework encompasses: • Strategic risks. • Financial risks. • Operational risks. • Regulatory risks. • Credit risks. • Liquidity risks. • Information technology risks. • Environmental and safety risks.
